weeks.title: Baseline, Setup, and JavaScript to Mastery
weeks.theme: You cannot fix what you have not measured. This week you establish honest baselines in all four tracks, then start the language work that everything else sits on.
weeks.deliverable: A public GitHub repo `senior-track-2027` with a daily log, plus baseline scores recorded for DSA, IELTS, and your current résumé.
weeks.milestone: IELTS test booked and paid for. Upwork + LinkedIn profiles live. First commit pushed.

weeks.title: TypeScript, Data Structures, and Algorithmic Fluency
weeks.theme: Senior interviews assume you can reason about types and complexity without thinking. This is the last week at the higher budget — use it.
weeks.deliverable: A typed, tested utility library on GitHub demonstrating generics, conditional types, and discriminated unions.
weeks.milestone: 25 LeetCode problems solved total. Big-O of every core data structure operation known from memory.

weeks.title: Node.js Internals and Express in Production
weeks.theme: The reduced budget starts today: 3 hours on weekdays, 6 on Saturday, Sunday off. Less time means less breadth, not less depth — everything scheduled from here is interview-critical.
weeks.deliverable: A layered Express API skeleton: routes → controllers → services → repositories, with structured logging and one central error handler.
weeks.milestone: You can explain the event loop phases from memory and demonstrate why one blocking handler freezes the whole server.

weeks.title: REST APIs and Async Resilience
weeks.theme: Two things separate a mid-level API from a senior one: a defensible resource design, and the assumption that every network call will fail.
weeks.deliverable: Full CRUD with cursor pagination, idempotency keys, ETags, and correct status codes for every branch.
weeks.milestone: You can name the right status code for all nine situations in the REST chapter table, and explain why 404-not-403 matters.

weeks.title: NestJS and Authentication — Project 1 Begins
weeks.theme: Auth is where most portfolio projects quietly fail an interview. Build it properly once and be able to defend every decision.
weeks.deliverable: PROJECT 1 starts: a multi-tenant SaaS API in NestJS with registration, login, email verification, and password reset.
weeks.milestone: Password auth that leaks nothing: no user enumeration on any endpoint, argon2id, constant-time comparison.

weeks.title: Tokens, OAuth, and Multi-Tenancy
weeks.theme: Refresh-token rotation with reuse detection is the single most impressive thing a mid-level candidate can demonstrate. It is also genuinely hard to get right.
weeks.deliverable: Access + refresh tokens with rotation and reuse detection, Google/GitHub OAuth with PKCE, RBAC, and tenant isolation enforced at the query layer.
weeks.milestone: You can explain refresh-token rotation and reuse detection out loud, in three minutes, without notes.

weeks.title: PostgreSQL and SQL to Interview Depth
weeks.theme: The highest-leverage skill for a backend senior. Most candidates know CRUD; almost none can read a query plan. That gap is your opportunity, and it is why this survived the budget cut intact.
weeks.deliverable: Project 1 on a real PostgreSQL schema with constraints and migrations, seeded with 1M+ rows for honest testing.
weeks.milestone: You can write a window-function query and a recursive CTE from memory.

weeks.title: Indexes, Query Plans — and Applications Open
weeks.theme: From Tuesday, job applications are a daily habit rather than an event. Applications take 4–8 weeks to convert, and there are 12 weeks left.
weeks.deliverable: Your three slowest queries taken under 50ms, with EXPLAIN ANALYZE output before and after in the README.
weeks.milestone: APPLICATIONS OPEN — 5 tailored applications every weekday from here to the deadline. No exceptions.

weeks.title: Redis, Caching, Queues, and Rate Limiting
weeks.theme: Everything this week answers one question: what do you do when it gets slow? Seniors answer with measurement, not guesses.
weeks.deliverable: Project 1 with cache-aside on the hottest endpoint, a BullMQ queue with retries and a DLQ, and distributed rate limiting.
weeks.milestone: p99 latency on your hottest endpoint cut by 10x, measured before and after.

weeks.title: Docker, CI/CD — Project 1 Goes Live
weeks.theme: A project that is not deployed is a hobby. This week Project 1 becomes a real, publicly reachable system with a URL you can put in an application.
weeks.deliverable: PROJECT 1 LIVE at a public HTTPS URL, auto-deploying on every push to main, with rollback.
weeks.milestone: A stranger can read your API docs and make a real authenticated request.

weeks.title: AWS Core, and the IELTS Ramp Begins
weeks.theme: Cloud fluency is what moves you from mid to senior on the salary band. Meanwhile the exam is three weeks out, so IELTS takes the evening slots from here.
weeks.deliverable: Project 1 re-deployed on AWS: ECS Fargate, RDS PostgreSQL, S3, ALB, CloudWatch alarms.
weeks.milestone: You can draw a 3-tier VPC from memory and explain why the database sits in a private subnet.

weeks.title: System Design Foundations and IELTS Intensive
weeks.theme: Design is a verbal skill, so every session ends with you speaking out loud. IELTS now takes both evening slots and half of Saturday — the exam is nine days away.
weeks.deliverable: Four system designs recorded, and IELTS Writing consistently hitting Band 7 structure.
weeks.milestone: You can run the full design framework — requirements, estimation, API, data model, high level, deep dive, bottlenecks — without notes.

weeks.title: IELTS Exam Week
weeks.theme: One goal this week. Engineering drops to maintenance and applications continue on autopilot. The exam is Saturday 14 November.
weeks.deliverable: IELTS taken. Band 7.5+ targeted.
weeks.milestone: EXAM SATURDAY 14 NOVEMBER. Walk out knowing you did every section the way you practised.

weeks.title: System Design Case Studies
weeks.theme: The named designs are interview currency, but the reasoning transfers to whatever they invent on the spot. With the exam behind you, evenings return to engineering.
weeks.deliverable: Five named system designs delivered fluently on camera, each under 30 minutes.
weeks.milestone: You can design Twitter, WhatsApp, or YouTube cold, handling follow-up pressure.

weeks.title: AI Engineering — RAG With Measured Retrieval
weeks.theme: The highest-paid specialisation you can add this year, and the one most candidates fake. Build a retrieval system that measurably works and you are in a small group.
weeks.deliverable: PROJECT 2: a RAG system with a 50-question golden set and a measured precision@5, not a demo that merely looks fine.
weeks.milestone: Retrieval precision improved from a measured baseline, with the number in your README.

weeks.title: Agents, MCP, and Shipping Project 2
weeks.theme: Agents are where the senior AI roles are. Ship Project 2 this week — it is the portfolio piece that makes you memorable.
weeks.deliverable: PROJECT 2 LIVE with a public demo, plus an agent with real tools and error recovery.
weeks.milestone: Two projects live with case studies. Portfolio page published with both.

weeks.title: Interview Execution
weeks.theme: Applications have been running for eleven weeks; interviews are landing now. Everything from here serves conversion, and new learning only fills gaps interviews have exposed.
weeks.deliverable: Project 1 infrastructure in Terraform, monitoring dashboards live, and a complete interview kit.
weeks.milestone: Two mock interviews with real humans completed. At least three active interview processes.

weeks.title: Converting: Final Rounds and Signed Work
weeks.theme: December opens. Companies want to close hires before the holidays — this is a hiring window, not a dead zone.
weeks.deliverable: Final-round interviews completed. Client work delivered and invoiced.
weeks.milestone: At least one offer in negotiation, or one signed client contract.

weeks.title: Offers, Negotiation, and the Holiday Window
weeks.theme: Most candidates stop this week. That is exactly why it works. Reduced volume, maintained consistency.
weeks.deliverable: Offers negotiated. Client retainer proposed.
weeks.milestone: Consistency held through the week everyone else quits.

weeks.title: Close-Out and the 2027 Setup
weeks.theme: Finish properly. Whatever the outcome, you end this with a portfolio, a band score, a pipeline, and a system that keeps working.
weeks.deliverable: The complete year-end review, a 2027 plan, and every loose end closed.
weeks.milestone: 1 JANUARY 2027 — job closed, or a pipeline that closes one within weeks.
